'''Gareth Owen Roberts''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] [[Learned Society of Wales|FLSW]] (born 1964) is a statistician and applied probabilist. He is [[Professor]] of [[Statistics]] in the Department of Statistics and Director of the Centre for Research in Statistical Methodology (CRiSM) at the [[University of Warwick]].<ref name=Warwick>{{cite web |url=http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/statistics/staff/academic/roberts/case8.6.8.pdf |archive-url=https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20090625183759/http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/statistics/staff/academic/roberts/case8.6.8.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=25 June 2009 |title=Researcher Biography |access-date=17 October 2009 }}</ref> He is an established authority on the stability of [[Markov chain]]s, especially applied to [[Markov chain Monte Carlo]] (MCMC) theory methodology for a wide range of latent statistical models with applications in [[spatial statistics]], [[infectious disease]] [[epidemiology]] and [[finance]].<ref>[http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/statistics/staff/academic/roberts/pub3.pdf Gareth Roberts Publications List]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://hcr3.isiknowledge.com/author.cgi?&link1=Search&link2=Search%20Results&AuthLastName=roberts&AuthFirstName=&AuthMiddleName=&AuthMailnstName=&CountryID=-1&DisciplineID=0&id=5059 |title=ISI Highly Cited Profile |access-date=17 October 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070519223724/http://hcr3.isiknowledge.com/author.cgi |archive-date=19 May 2007 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

==Education==
Roberts was educated at [[Liverpool Blue Coat School]] and [[Jesus College, Oxford]], graduating in 1985 in [[Mathematics]]<ref name=ISI>{{cite web|url=http://hcr3.isiknowledge.com/author.cgi?&link1=Search&link2=Search%20Results&AuthLastName=roberts&AuthFirstName=&AuthMiddleName=&AuthMailnstName=&CountryID=-1&DisciplineID=0&id=5059|title=ISI Highly Cited Profile|access-date=17 October 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070519223724/http://hcr3.isiknowledge.com/author.cgi|archive-date=19 May 2007|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> and subsequently went on to complete in 1988 a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] thesis on ''Some boundary hitting problems for diffusion processes''<ref>{{cite web | url = http://encore.lib.warwick.ac.uk/iii/encore/record/C__Rb1455392 | title = Some boundary hitting problems for diffusion processes | publisher = University of Warwick Library | access-date = 25 January 2013}}</ref>  under the supervision of Saul Jacka at the [[University of Warwick]].

==Career==
Following his PhD, Roberts held various academic positions at the [[University of Nottingham]], the [[University of Cambridge]] and [[Lancaster University]] before returning to the [[University of Warwick]].<ref name=Warwick/> He was a [[Fellow (Oxbridge)|Fellow]] of [[St Catharine's College, Cambridge]] from 1992 to 1998.

Roberts is a talented [[contract bridge|tournament bridge]] player, whose achievements include winning the Great Northern Swiss Pairs in 1997,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ebu.co.uk/node/2250 |title=Great Northern Swiss Pairs |website=[[English Bridge Union]] |access-date=4 December 2016}}</ref> and the Garden Cities Trophy in 2008 and 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ebu.co.uk/node/442 |title=The Garden Cities Trophy – the history |website=[[English Bridge Union]] |access-date=4 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ebu.co.uk/node/1025 |title=Coventry and North Warwickshire Bridge Club win Garden Cities |website=[[English Bridge Union]] |access-date=4 December 2016}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
*1995 – Raybould Fellowship
*1997 – [[Royal Statistical Society]]'s [[Guy Medal|Guy medal in Bronze]]
*1999 – [[Rollo Davidson Prize]] of the [[University of Cambridge]]
*2004 – [[ISI highly cited researcher]]<ref name=ISI/> (Mathematics: Ranked 16th <ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/may-june2002/sw_may-june2002_page2.htm|title=ISI Highly Cited Statistics – Mathematics}}</ref>)
*2008 – [[Royal Statistical Society]]'s [[Guy Medal|Guy medal in Silver]]
*2009 – [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] Medallion
*2010 – Editor of [[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society]] (Series B)
*2013 – Elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]]
*2019 - Elected a [[Learned Society of Wales|Fellow of the Learned Society of Wales]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wales |first=The Learned Society of |title=Gareth Owen Roberts |url=https://www.learnedsociety.wales/fellow/gareth-owen-roberts/ |access-date=2023-08-31 |website=The Learned Society of Wales |language=en-US}}</ref>

His nomination to become a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2013|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2013]] reads:
{{quote|text="Gareth Roberts is distinguished for his work spanning Applied Probability, Bayesian Statistics and Computational Statistics. He has made fundamental contributions to the theory, methodology and application of Markov chain Monte Carlo and related methods in Statistics. He has developed crucial convergence and stability theory, constructed a theory of optimal scaling for [[Metropolis–Hastings algorithm]]s, and has introduced and explored the theory of adaptive MCMC algorithms. He has made pioneering contributions to infinite dimensional simulation problems and inference in stochastic processes. His work has already found practical application in the study of epidemics such as [[Avian Influenza]] and [[Foot-and-mouth disease|Foot and Mouth disease]]."<ref name="frs">[http://royalsociety.org/people/gareth-roberts Professor Gareth Roberts FRS]</ref>}}

*2015 – [[Wolfson Research Merit Award]] from the Royal Society <ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2015/07/wolfson-research-merit-awards-july/|title=Royal Society announces recipients of prestigious Wolfson Research Merit Awards|publisher= Royal Society|access-date= 26 November 2018}}</ref>
